findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous authentication path
findings.body: TagDevice used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout. It now runs synchronously inside Authenticate, so every anonymous request whose device is not in the local cache waits on DB writes. With a device limit configured it also runs a COUNT query first. This adds latency to anonymous requests. A slow or failing database now delays anonymous authentication, and the request context's cancellation can abort the tag.

findings.title: Cache set before DB write lets rejected devices bypass the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the cache key before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the call returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key stays cached. For the next ~29 minutes, requests from that device hit the cache, return nil, and authenticate successfully. Only the first request is rejected, so the limit is effectively not enforced. The key should be cached only after a successful write, or removed when the write fails.

findings.title: Racy count-then-insert allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts, without a transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit can be exceeded. Each new device also adds a full COUNT query.

findings.title: Existing device with an unchanged-timestamp update reports limit reached
findings.body: updateDevice treats rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, RowsAffected by default counts only rows that actually changed. An existing device re-tagged with the same IP, user agent and second-precision timestamp therefore returns 0 rows and is wrongly rejected even though it is already a registered device.

findings.title: Store construction bypasses DI; wire providers likely broken
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB and builds the store itself, instead of receiving the injected anonstore.AnonStore. ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an extra int64 argument, which wire cannot provide. Any wire set that still references anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore or binds AnonStore will fail to build, and the change was not updated in this PR.
